name: Stella Hull
life: “I first measured pavement slopes with a marble and a plumb line.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Stella takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: My wheelchair fits the new turn. I brought the planners cake and asked them to hear the old riders too.
appearance: Stella has brown hair pinned away from the temples, one cheek that creases before the other, and a favorite piece of clothing, an unlined tan jacket. It usually goes with a small enamel bird on the lapel. When somebody else has the floor, Stella holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Stella is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Stella asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To preserve the easier wheelchair turn and hear the displaced riders.
family: Dario Flint is Stella’s second cousin. A relative kept reporting household news on postcards long after everybody could afford to phone. Reading one takes the family back to an ordinary morning rather than a big event. Stella saves apparently unimportant details. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Dario says, “I let children freeze the turrets in my cart.”
connections: Alicia Nielsen. An old-stop regular walks the new wheelchair turn alongside its advocate. Also in the story is Lou Arnett (route planner).

reactions.situation: A driver goes past the old stop in the rain
reactions.response: Stella stays with the stranded rider and helps check the next usable stop.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Stella asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.

reactions.response: Stella accepts only after finding out whether the person doing the regular work can come too.
